about: Albany Distilling Company’s rums carry the name of the Quackenbush Still House, Albany’s first distillery, established in the mid-18th century a short distance from where the company began in 2011. Founders John Curtin and Matthew Jager, two teachers, opened what became the city’s first licensed distillery since Prohibition, and rum has been part of the work from the start: the house recipe follows the old still house’s methods, updated with modern equipment, better yeast and a cleaner water supply.

The Quackenbush rums are made from fancy-grade Caribbean molasses and distilled on a hybrid pot-and-column still in Albany. This bottling is the navy-strength expression. “Navy strength” traditionally means rum bottled at about 57% alcohol, the strength at which, as the old story goes, rum spilled on the Royal Navy’s gunpowder would not stop it from igniting. It is the most concentrated way to taste the distillery’s rum, and a classic choice for tiki drinks and punches.
title: Albany Distilling Co. Quackenbush Navy Strength Rum
